1.tell: two prose options vs two numeric; on hard rational/radical equations the prose 'no solution' is the standard key and the numeric pair is the extraneous-root lure

2.tell: 9 is the hub: 3 = sqrt(9), 10 = 9+1 (off-by-one slip); 37 is unrelated to everything, so it is padding

3.tell: 3 generates the others (6 = 2x3, 4 = 3+1, 0 = drop-a-term slip); 0 is the classic throwaway

4.tell: perfectly symmetric +/-2, +/-3 set, no structural cue; guessed the positive of the larger-magnitude twin

5.tell: arithmetic run 100/200/300/400; picked the lower median, which is where keys sit in centred option sets

6.tell: 6 is the product hub (2 and 3 are its factors, 9 = 3^2 one step further out)

7.tell: -10/3 = -4 + 2/3, i.e. the only value combining the other two non-zero options; 0 is the lone throwaway

8.tell: 1/2/3 is a filler run; 6 is the odd one out by magnitude and equals 3! / 1x2x3

9.tell: 11 has an explicit sign twin (-11); the sign-twin pair is where the key normally lives, and the positive one is the un-slipped member

10.tell: 1,2,3,4 run with no other structure; took the lower median of the run

11.tell: +/-3 sign-twin pair marks the key; 5 and 2 are the sum/difference decoys

12.tell: 2,3,4 is a tight filler run; 7 = 3+4 is the odd one out by size and the only value not one edit from its neighbours

13.tell: all four are built from digits 2,3,7; 7/3 has both a reciprocal decoy (3/7) and a denominator-slip decoy (7/2), so it is the hub

14.tell: only option with a fraction (13/3) among three integers; on hard Advanced Math the ugly value is usually the key and the round ones are the slips

15.tell: no structure; picked -2 as the interior value of the spread (-5,-2,1,4)

16.tell: +/-3 sign-twin pair; picked the positive member, with 2 and -1 as unrelated padding

17.tell: form alone decides it: 0.12 is a rate not a multiplier, 0.99 is an unrelated base, and 12m vs m/12 is the unit inversion; 8000(0.88)^(m/12) is the only internally coherent expression

18.tell: 9 is the hub: 3 = sqrt(9), 36 = 4x9, 4 = the other factor; the derived values surround it

19.tell: 4,5,6 arithmetic run with 21 as the outlier; key at the median of the run

20.tell: 22/23 adjacent pair is an off-by-one slip around the key, and 45 = 22+23 confirms the pair is load-bearing; took the upper member

21.tell: full +/- and x4 symmetry (+/-6, +/-24); no cue, guessed the negative large value that a sign-slip design would protect

22.tell: +/-1, +/-7 symmetric set, no cue; guessed the positive large-magnitude value

23.tell: +/-7, +/-13 symmetric set; 13 is the larger magnitude and the less guessable-looking value

24.tell: doubling pairs (4,8) and (5,10); 8 sits interior and is reachable from both pairs, 10 is the lone round decoy
